title: The Devil's Star
subtitle: Jo Nesbø, 2003 · Harry Hole #5
blurb: In a summer-stifled Oslo, Harry Hole investigates a sequence of murders marked by a pentagram motif while his career and sobriety are collapsing. The case also brings to a head Harry’s long-running conflict with corrupt detective Tom Waaler.

factions.label: Oslo Police Investigation
factions.description: Police officers and specialists working the Oslo murder case, formally or reluctantly.

factions.label: Harry's Personal Circle
factions.description: People outside the case who anchor, challenge, or expose Harry’s private life.

factions.label: Waaler Corruption Plot
factions.description: The concealed criminal thread surrounding Tom Waaler and earlier police deaths.

factions.label: Pentagram Murder Case
factions.description: The victims and staged pattern that drive the novel’s main investigation.

characters.name: Harry Hole
characters.description: Harry is the alcoholic but gifted Oslo detective at the center of the investigation. The novel culminates in his exposure of Tom Waaler’s corruption and a decisive break in that long-running conflict.
characters.name_evidence: Oslo detective investigating pentagram murders while facing dismissal

characters.name: Tom Waaler
characters.description: Waaler is Harry’s polished, dangerous colleague and the hidden criminal antagonist of the police-corruption arc. His confrontation with Harry brings the Waaler storyline to its resolution, and Waaler dies by the end of the novel.
characters.name_evidence: Detective assigned as Harry's partner, later exposed as corrupt

characters.name: Bjarne Møller
characters.description: Møller is Harry’s boss, caught between institutional discipline and his knowledge of Harry’s investigative value. He gives Harry limited room to work despite Harry’s worsening professional position.
characters.name_evidence: Police superior handling Harry's dismissal and murder assignment

characters.name: Beate Lønn
characters.description: Beate assists the investigation with her distinctive memory and recognition abilities. She is part of the police network that helps Harry follow evidence beyond official appearances.
characters.name_evidence: Police specialist aiding the investigation with facial recognition skills

characters.name: Rakel Fauke
characters.description: Rakel is Harry’s love interest and the person most closely tied to his hope for a stable private life. Her plans involving Oleg sharpen the emotional cost of Harry’s alcoholism and police obsession.
characters.name_evidence: Harry's lover, considering life away from Oslo with Oleg

characters.name: Oleg Fauke
characters.description: Oleg is Rakel’s son and a child Harry deeply cares for. His bond with Harry makes the possible loss of Rakel’s household a central personal stake.
characters.name_evidence: Rakel's son, central to Harry's fragile domestic hopes

characters.name: Ellen Gjelten
characters.description: Ellen is Harry’s former police partner, already dead before the main action but still central to Harry’s pursuit of the truth. Her murder is tied to Waaler’s concealed criminal activity.
characters.name_evidence: Harry's murdered former partner, tied to Waaler's hidden crimes

characters.name: Ståle Aune
characters.description: Aune is Harry’s psychologist friend and sounding board. He helps frame Harry’s behavior and the mental pressures surrounding the investigation.
characters.name_evidence: Psychologist friend Harry consults amid the murder investigation

characters.name: Øystein Eikeland
characters.description: Øystein is one of Harry’s loyal civilian friends. He is part of the informal support network that keeps Harry functioning when his drinking and isolation worsen.
characters.name_evidence: Taxi-driver friend who helps Harry during alcoholic relapses

characters.name: Pentagram murder victims
characters.description: The murdered women form the apparent pattern of the case, with pentagram imagery and staged clues pushing the investigation forward. They are grouped here to avoid misnaming individual victims.
characters.name_evidence: Women killed across Oslo in the five-point-star pattern
